newsitem.title: UK: UK pledges to improve ties with European Union.
newsitem.headline: UK pledges to improve ties with European Union.

text.p: New British Foreign Secretary Robin Cook said on Friday that one of his priorities was to improve relations with the European Union which suffered grievously during the last years of Conservative rule.

"Labour's job is to give Britain back a strong voice in world affairs after many years in which that voice has not been heard above the noisy divisions within the Conservative party," he said minutes after being appointed to his post.
The Conservatives of John Major crashed to a humiliating election defeat on Thursday, in part caused by deep splits over policy towards the European Union.

Relations with the EU plummeted to rock bottom last year after the 15-nation bloc slapped an export ban on British beef exports amid fears that mad cow disease could spread to humans. Major briefly suspended all cooperation with the EU in protest.

Cook, speaking to reporters outside the number 10 Downing Street residence of new Labour Prime Minister Tony Blair, said he wanted to make Britain a leading player in a Europe of independent nation states.
"We know we can better shape the direction of Europe if Britain takes its rightful place in the driving seat of Europe, instead of heckling from the back seat," he said.

Labour has gradually changed its position on Europe to reflect that of the Conservatives -- retaining the right not to join a European single currency and promising to hold a referendum before any such decision was taken.
Cook, who like most of his colleagues has no ministerial experience, denied he would be swamped by crucial forthcoming negotiations over the future of the EU.
"We have been tracking those negotiations for well over a year now, we have a number of sister parties throughout Europe, most of them in government," he later told BBC radio.
"We've kept in touch with them and we know what the score is. We know what are policies are, we can hit the ground running and that's what we plan to do."

Cook reiterated Labour's pledge to use British embassies to promote trade to secure jobs at home and said he would try to gain international respect for Britain's commitment to peace-keeping missions around the world.
